steps.why: Flat is easier to read at high zoom.

steps.question: How soft are shadows?
steps.why: No shadows; borders do the work.

steps.why: The dimmed page makes the dialog obvious.

pick: shadow.none: We use no shadow for menus and dialogs in order to show their height without a cast shade: the scale gives no layer a step here. The missing shade does this by leaving the layer to its border and the dimmed page behind it. So a dialog stands out at any zoom with no blur to read through, because nothing rises (elevation.roles) and there are no shadows (elevation.values).
darkPick: shadow.none: We use the light pick for the dark overlay elevation in order to keep the height it sets, and the step does this by the same means, so the dark overlay elevation and the light pick never differ, because the step reads the same in dark (theming.values).

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest
, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
darkPick: neutral.300: We use the step above the raised surface for dividers and card borders in dark in order to give separation on every surface a line meets, menus included. The line does this by staying lighter than each surface, lowest
, on surface.raised. So rows and cards stay apart on content and in menus, because lines separate groups (elevation.definition) and dark ships as standard (theming.values).

steps.why: Items in one group sit 16px apart, not the 12px tight gap: generous space between fields stops mis-taps.

pick: radius.6: We use a 6px corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a calm, clear tone, by brand convention. A slight radius does this by softening the edge while the box keeps a clear rectangle. So every field and button reads plainly as something to use, because the brand is calm and clear (brand.q1) and corners are slightly rounded (shape.values).

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
darkPick: neutral.50: We use a step darker than content for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets:
on surface.default and
on surface.raised. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads
on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).
